title: An Efficient Vth-Tilting PUF Design in 3nm GAA and 8nm FinFET Technologies
problem: Physically unclonable functions require process-mismatch entropy extraction while maintaining stability across process-voltage-temperature corners; conventional PUF enrollment requires screening across multiple PVT conditions, increasing test time and cost.
method: Standard-cell-only PUF extracting entropy from threshold-voltage mismatches in inverting cells, with Vth-tilting scheme supporting efficient enrollment by screening at nominal V/T only; includes power-gating (BTI mitigation), balanced sampler (side-channel reduction), and laser-attack detection.

title: Telos: A Dataflow Accelerator for Sparse Triangular Solver of Partial Differential Equations
problem: Sparse triangular solve (SpTRSV) dominates runtime in preconditioned iterative solvers for PDE-derived linear systems due to loop-carried dependencies that severely limit parallelism. Prior accelerators cannot simultaneously achieve high parallelism and good data locality for structured sparsity from stencil-based PDE discretizations.
method: Telos is a dataflow accelerator that exploits structured (stencil-pattern) sparsity in SpTRSV. A plane-parallel pipelining technique maps dependent computations across processing elements (PEs) while preserving data locality within each plane. A cross-plane communication aggregation technique reorganizes inter-plane data transfers into systolic flows, enabling pipelined resolution of loop-carried dependencies with minimal stall overhead. Computation is overlapped with memory accesses to hide latency.

title: A Simulation Framework for Workload Management in Hybrid Quantum-HPC Cloud System
problem: Hybrid quantum-HPC cloud platforms require workload management across classical and quantum resources, introducing challenges in device variability, noise-prone quantum processors, and distributed orchestration.
method: HybridCloudSim simulation framework designed to model hybrid quantum-HPC cloud environments. Comprehensive survey of state-of-the-art scheduling, resource allocation, and workflow management techniques. Taxonomy categorizing approaches by strategy, allocation model, orchestration mechanism, and metrics.

title: Analysis and Design Considerations for MASH of Noise Shaped SAR ADCs
problem: This brief analyses the residue amplifier non-idealities and design considerations for noise shaping (NS) successive approximation register (SAR) based multi stage noise shaping (MASH) analog to digital converter (ADC) architecture
method: design considerations for noise shaping (NS) successive approximation register (SAR) based multi stage noise shaping (MASH) analog to digital converter (ADC) architecture

title: 32.4 A Dual-LC-Resonant Isolated DC-DC Converter Achieving 65.4% Peak Efficiency and Inherent Backscattering
problem: Integrated isolated DC-DC converters (with on-chip transformers) suffer from low peak efficiency (~52%) due to TX LC-oscillator losses, RX full-bridge rectifier losses, and parasitic transformer elements. Traditional feedback from RX to TX requires costly digital isolators; alternative RX-only regulation approaches sacrifice efficiency (<37%).
method: Dual-LC-resonant topology optimizes TX and RX resonators independently. TX uses optimized LC oscillator; RX employs resonant rectification (not full-bridge) to reduce rectifier losses. Inherent backscattering mechanism enables RX-to-TX feedback via modulating load impedance on resonator, eliminating need for digital isolator while maintaining RX-side regulation.

title: EIGEN: Enabling Efficient 3DIC Interconnect with Heterogeneous Dual-Layer Network-on-Active-Interposer
problem: Chiplet-based 3DIC systems using active interposers struggle with heterogeneous and high-load inter-chiplet network traffic patterns because their interconnects are tightly coupled to top-die designs, preventing flexible topology adaptation and causing high latency and traffic congestion.
method: EIGEN implements a heterogeneous dual-layer interconnect on the active interposer: an application-aware switch-programmable layer (AspLayer) for static topology optimization and a dynamic packet-routing layer (DynLayer) for adaptive traffic management. A reinforcement learning (RL)-based path routing framework is trained with a state space covering topology, network, and memory metrics, with reward defined as the product of average packet latency and link utilization. The two layers cooperate to route inter-chiplet traffic with reduced hops and congestion.

title: 34.1 A 65fsrms-Jitter and -272dB-FoMjitter, N 10.1GHz Fractional-N Digital PLL with a Quantization-Error-Compensating BBPD and an Orthogonal-Polynomial LMS Calibration
problem: Fractional-N digital PLLs suffer from quantization errors in ΔΣ modulators that dominate in-band phase noise; digital-to-time converters (DTCs) mitigate ΔΣ Q-error but introduce thermal noise proportional to delay, creating a power-jitter tradeoff that degrades overall FoM.
method: A fractional-N digital PLL with a bang-bang phase detector (BBPD) that directly compensates for ΔΣ modulator quantization errors, eliminating the need for a high-power DTC. An orthogonal-polynomial LMS calibration algorithm adaptively adjusts quantization compensation across process, voltage, and temperature variations.

title: PROCA: Programmable Probabilistic Processing Unit Architecture with Accept/Reject Prediction & Multicore Pipelining for Causal Inference
problem: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms for probabilistic programming and causal inference are extremely compute-intensive and inherently sequential, preventing effective parallelization on CPUs and GPUs; existing MCMC accelerators are not programmable across arbitrary posterior distribution forms.
method: PROCA is a programmable MCMC processing unit using processing-in-memory (PIM) function units to generate Markov chain samples. A novel accept/reject prediction methodology predicts whether a proposed sample will be accepted before completing full posterior evaluation, enabling multi-core pipelining: compute for the next sample begins before the current accept/reject decision finalizes. The architecture is programmable to support arbitrary posterior distribution forms compatible with software probabilistic programming frameworks (e.g., PyMC). Implemented using commercial process development kits and validated on 9 benchmarks spanning PyMC tutorials, single-variable problems, and real-world causal inference tasks.

title: ENABLING AI Infrastructure: Tomahawk Ultra - Ultra Low Latency, High Bandwidth Ethernet Switch for HPC & AI/ML applications
problem: AI/ML data centers require ultra-low-latency, high-bandwidth switching to support collective operations and distributed training; Tomahawk Ultra targets sub-microsecond latency Ethernet switching.
method: Tomahawk Ultra implements high-radix Ethernet switching with optimized packet pipeline, cut-through forwarding, and minimal queue depth for ultra-low latency, combined with advanced congestion control and in-switch QoS to prioritize AI collective traffic.

title: ZRAID: Leveraging Zone Random Write Area (ZRWA) for Alleviating Partial Parity Tax in ZNS RAID
problem: ZNS SSD RAID systems must manage partial parity for incomplete stripes; prior approaches log partial parity in reserved zones, creating throughput bottlenecks and exacerbating write amplification that reduces SSD lifetime.
method: ZRAID exploits the Zone Random Write Area (ZRWA), a small random-write buffer region within ZNS SSDs, to buffer and consolidate partial parity in-place before committing full stripes to sequential zones. By using ZRWA as a transient parity staging area, ZRAID avoids persistent partial parity logging to reserved zones, eliminating the associated throughput bottleneck and write amplification. The system coordinates ZRWA usage across multiple ZNS drives to maintain RAID consistency.

title: Topology-Aware Virtualization over Inter-Core Connected Neural Processing Units
problem: Inter-core connected NPUs (e.g., Graphcore IPU, Tenstorrent) require large hardware resources, leading to poor utilization when tasks have imbalanced resource requirements, yet no prior virtualization work accounts for their hardware topology (NoC routing, SRAM-centric cores). Existing MIG-style monolithic virtualization ignores inter-core communication structure and therefore delivers suboptimal performance when multiple workloads share the device.
method: vNPU introduces three integrated techniques: (1) NPU route virtualization redirects instruction and data flow from virtual NPU core IDs to physical cores, constructing a virtual topology over the physical NoC fabric; (2) NPU memory virtualization uses SRAM-centric and NoC-aware address translation to minimize translation stalls and maximize effective memory bandwidth; (3) best-effort topology mapping enumerates candidate virtual topologies and selects the mapping that best balances resource utilization against end-to-end performance for the collocated workload mix. A prototype is validated on FPGA (Chipyard+FireSim) and on a simulator (DCRA).

title: AskHPC: A ChatBot for High Performance Computing User Support
problem: Exascale HPC systems are increasingly heterogeneous with complex tools, configurations, and best practices. Documentation is scattered across multimodal sources. Users struggle to find accurate information efficiently.
method: LLM-based chatbot (AskHPC) with curated knowledge base and RAG framework. Dual-context strategy: retrieved content (e.g., code blocks) + LLM-generated semantics. Modality-aware document parsing for multimodal sources. Real user study evaluation.

title: UltraAttn: Efficiently Parallelizing Attention through Hierarchical Context-Tiling
problem: Long-context comprehension requires context parallelism and irregular block-sparse attention, but existing methods suffer from poor scalability due to striped partitioning causing high communication traffic and ring-based patterns limiting kernel granularity.
method: UltraAttn implements hierarchical context tiling at node and device levels to reduce communication cost. It applies kernel-level tiling to balance kernel overlap and device utilization. An ILP-based runtime further optimizes distributed attention latency.

title: Preserving CUDA Syntax for SYCL Portability: A Thin C++ Abstraction without Kernel Migration
problem: Large-scale scientific applications must support multiple GPU architectures (NVIDIA, Intel), but converting CUDA code to SYCL requires significant effort and risks introducing bugs. Existing approaches either require full code translation or accept performance penalties.
method: Thin C++ abstraction layer preserving original CUDA kernel syntax and launch style while providing SYCL compatibility. Mechanical 'functorization' process converts CUDA to SYCL without full source translation. Evaluated on CRK-HACC (N-body cosmology code) across Polaris (NVIDIA) and Aurora (Intel) systems. Retains architecture-specific optimizations.

title: Modelling Load Imbalance In Shared Memory Multicore Systems
problem: Memory bandwidth saturates with increasing core count; mainstream performance models assume homogeneous per-core memory traffic, leading to inaccurate time estimates when traffic is inhomogeneous
method: New performance model targeting inhomogeneous per-core memory traffic; requires only three hardware parameters; demonstrates advantage over mainstream bandwidth-based strategy

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper GPU Lossy Compression for HPC Can Be Versatile and Ultra-Fast
problem: Artifact reproducibility and evaluation of published SC research requires systematic evaluation against artifact evaluation criteria. This report documents reproducibility assessment of GPU lossy compression work.
method: Artifact evaluation following SC25 Artifact Description and Evaluation appendix criteria. Reproducibility committee member conducts independent artifact assessment.
